changes: packages/main/src/core/review-escalation.ts: eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade no longer rewrites a superseded host verdict onto the current material when a verdict of the same runId and overlapping host identity is already there natively, and treats EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH as no-signal rather than a match. packages/main/src/core/host-independence.ts: normalizeIdentity is exported so the collision guard and groupByIndependentHost share one identity rule instead of restating it. Two registered red tests added under packages/main/tests/red/.
usage: No command changes. lattice review_escalation_status and the review-assurance floor now count a quorum that genuinely exists at the current material instead of scoring it 0/N. The two guards run automatically as part of lattice validate.
expectedOutcome: A complete 3x2 quorum at the current material counts as 3/3 valid rounds even when a superseded quorum for the same runIds exists at an older material sharing its storyFilesHash, and a registered test permanently guards that.
actualTranscript: red-f88e-quorum-downgrade-collision.mjs exited 1 before the fix with "DOWNGRADE COLLISION: ... counted as 0/3 valid rounds" and six manufactured duplicate host/session/key identity reasons; it exits 0 after the fix with all twelve fixture verdicts still distinct on disk and the non-vacuity assertion (current-material quorum alone already yields 3/3) satisfied. red-f88e-downgrade-non-regression.mjs exits 0, pinning that a lone superseded verdict is still downgraded with its mandatory advisory and preserved originalMaterialDigest, that genuine same-identity verdicts recorded natively at the current material still invalidate the round, that two EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH values never authorise a downgrade, and that a mixed-case hostId cannot slip the guard. Every guard was bite-verified by downgrading the compiled dist and confirming the matching assertion fires, then restoring. Three reviewer lanes passed the current round (quality RP-003, test-coverage RP-004, concept RP-005) with 0 open findings, and the review-assurance floor reports satisfied with quorum 3/3 rounds x 2 hosts.
outcomeDiff: No difference: the red test flips from 0/3 to 3/3 exactly as expected, and the floor counts the quorum.
limitations: The fix removes the fabrication at its source only. Quorum runIds remain fixed and not round-scoped (option B, deliberately rejected), so a fresh review round still reuses the same runIds; that is now harmless because a superseded set can no longer collide with a live one, but it means the gate remedy text for stale_closeout_review still does not by itself mint new quorum runs. Already-recorded verdicts of past stories are not retroactively repaired.
pitfalls: Three reviewer findings were real defects I had introduced, each caught by a different lane and each fixed rather than accepted: an unreachable inner EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH branch (F-001); a literal NUL byte used as the identity-key separator, which made file(1) classify review-escalation.ts as binary and made plain grep skip it entirely - a silent blind spot for this repo grep-based scanners, and the cause of an earlier grep returning nothing that I had wrongly dismissed as a tooling glitch; and F-002, where hostIdentityKeys compared with trim-only while groupByIndependentHost folds case, so a differently-cased hostId would have slipped the guard and reproduced the very collision being fixed. The lesson that generalises: when a new guard must agree with an existing comparison, import that function rather than restating the rule in a comment. Also note each source fix invalidates the evidence and the reviewer passes, so batch corrections before re-running lanes, and refresh evidence BEFORE the reviewers rather than after.
